issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.stock (the shared stock attribute). Problem statement (lines 70-71) tells students to initialize instance fields ("These should be initialized to default values ... in the constructor of SealSaloon"), implying initialization of stock in the constructor. Later in the same problem statement (lines 77-80) it explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and final (shared across instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is contradictory and will confuse students. The reference solution declares and initializes the static final stock at its declaration (SealSaloon.java, line declaring "private static final Stock stock = new Stock();"). This inconsistency between where/how stock should be initialized (constructor vs. static declaration) is misleading and may cause students to implement the field incorrectly or get compilation/semantic errors when following the instructions literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement. Either: (A) require stock to be an instance (non-static) final field and instruct students to initialize it in the SealSaloon constructor, or (B) keep stock as static final and explicitly instruct students to initialize it at the field declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem text to state explicitly: "The stock attribute is static final (shared across all SealSaloon instances); initialize it at its declaration or in a static initializer. The constructor should initialize instance fields like orders." This preserves the intended design and removes ambiguity.
